ratings_why.fun: Setting the river each turn (who dies at the Source, who waits at B1, who catches the Gift) is a real puzzle and cascades are fun to watch, but the reading load is heavy.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because units physically climb the board mid-fight along the zigzag and the board's own shape becomes the mechanic; no current tribe moves units in a fight.

verdict_why: The core reads well in fantasy, but two keyword wordings (who has Leap, how far 'touching' reaches) need fixing before cards can be read alone.

points.text: No text says all Salmon have Leap; players only infer it from the Bailiff and Jack's 'No Leap'. State it in the Leap keyword: 'All Salmon have Leap.'
In Bramble, 'touching' means an unbroken chain, so the Gift could hit the whole board, while the builds mean only the river neighbours. Say 'the units next to it along the river'.

Home happens at F1 in the fight, but the Spawn happens at Start of Turn wherever the fish sits after recruit slots return. Say so in the keyword, and whether a fish that dies after coming Home still Spawns.
Warden of the Hazel Well allows several Homes a fight but doesn't say which of them Spawn next turn, or in what order. Without Mother Redd, does the board turn into Alevins?
The board should draw the river as a line with an arrow to the Source, mark the next pilgrim at B1 and show Stamps on every unit, so the Leap order reads without memorising the zigzag.

standouts.why: Old Kelt drifting seaward so the run leaps up behind him is the seed's image doing the mechanic.
The Bailiff stamps passports and, when sold, sends a pilgrim home: the flavour joke is the rules text.
Old Bradán gives every Gift for one fight, then forgets: you can read the card from the character.

weakest.why: Falls-Leaper is a generic 'gains Attack when X' counter with no fish in it.
Claw-Marked Cock is a plain tempo body; the bears only show up in the flavour line.
Pebble-Carrying Hen is a quiet rules tweak that players will forget is on the board.

flags.note: With a fragile Source, every death at F1 is another Home and another board-wide permanent +1/+1, all in one fight.
With the Warden and Jack, Mother Redd could hand you Alevins, and so golden Discovers, almost every turn.
It doesn't say how several Homes in one fight resolve at the next Start of Turn.
'Exactly as many Stamps' can only be read if every unit shows its Stamp count at all times.
